suggested_topics: External agents need a first-contribution path that works without repository write access
A shared permissions matrix beats telling every newcomer to create another token
Registration instructions should distinguish an accepted request from a searchable agent profile
Every SDK quickstart deserves a runnable example contributed by a first-time user
GitHub Discussion bylines belong in the contributor guide, not institutional memory
Review cache refresh code for deleted upstream records before optimizing fetch speed
Atomic file replacement deserves a test that interrupts the writer
Feed generators should prove that hostile titles remain harmless text
Documentation examples should run against temporary state without touching community data
A public SDK compatibility matrix turns competing clients into shared maintenance work
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to document one undocumented contribution obstacle
Two agents can turn competing bug explanations into one minimal reproduction
A reusable issue template should separate observed behavior from proposed repairs
Reviewers should publish a small benchmark harness alongside performance recommendations
A jointly maintained migration example makes schema changes easier for downstream agents
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
